executiveSummary: GM0163's 2025 identity, centre, population, 39 neighbourhoods, five BAG places, 23 settlement labels, two stations and six NWB-derived border links are coherent, and the full deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The generic named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset sustains direct inundation stress 0.821737 from T+24 through T+72, assigns 9,751 affected people-equivalent and accumulates 767,510.247 deprived person-hours without selecting a Regge, local brook, rainfall, sewer, terrain, control or recession event. The adopted 2025 Twente profile says the high-ground region has no dike rings or primary defences and only limited, short-lived local flooding along the Regge/Dinkel during heavy or prolonged rain. Suppress the false major-river amplitude while keeping Regge, hillslope, groundwater, sewer and indirect IJssel-region effects Unknown until a governed event is selected. The mobility graph separately omits the N35 in both directions and its 493 m Salland-Twentetunnel, the only long tunnel in Twente and a combined road/rail dependency monitored around the clock; neither scheduled rail nor six secondary logical edges substitute for it. Eight unrelated hazards share one exact 39-neighbourhood order. A controlled T+11 ignition at [6.42, 52.39], inside both the official 5,200 ha Sallandse Heuvelrug combustible polygon and neighbourhood Hellendoorn, produces direct fire 0.763379 and 17,334 affected people-equivalent while its source neighbourhood ranks only 14th. Public climate, sewer, water-control, transport, care, education, antenna, air-quality and grid-planning evidence can improve the first-72-hour exercise, but it does not establish live topology, occupancy, capacity, backup, incident state or restoration. Unknown, NoData and zero matched records must never be shown as zero or safe, and exact local consequences remain synthetic until source-valid support is approved.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0163 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0163 as Hellendoorn and reports 36,213 residents, density 263/km², 24.3% aged 65 or older and 4,441 one-person households; the generated centre [6.465439454324874, 52.3843553860018] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Thirty-nine published neighbourhood rows in nine districts sum to 36,190 residents, 23 below the municipality total (-0.064%); households sum to 15,040 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 8,790. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 36,213 without rewriting observations.

BAG supplies five active woonplaatsen—Daarle, Daarlerveen, Haarle, Hellendoorn and Nijverdal—and BRT supplies 23 labels: six woonkernen, fifteen buurtschappen and two gehuchten. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT are edition-based CC BY 4.0; labels are not hazard, catchment or service footprints.

Home-value/housing, benefit, density and doctor/supermarket-distance fields cover 38/39 neighbourhoods and cars per household 36/39; district-heating and charging cover 0/39. Publisher null, suppressed and non-applicable values remain NoData. Annual residents are observed context, not incident-time presence or individual vulnerability.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Adopted Regionaal Risicoprofiel Twente 2025 and Regionaal Crisisplan 2026
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile 2025, adopted 23 April 2026; crisis plan effective 10 July 2026
supports: The formally adopted profile describes Twente as relatively high, without dike rings or primary flood defences. The Regge and Dinkel can cause limited, short-lived local flooding during prolonged/heavy rain; drought and reliance on rainfall are more material. Possible indirect effects of an IJssel flood were still being assessed in 2025/2026.

For Hellendoorn it specifically identifies the 493 m combined N35 road/rail Salland-Twentetunnel, the only long tunnel in Twente, and the Sallandse Heuvelrug's elevated nature-fire risk from dry vegetation and wind; a very large April 2022 fire burned more than 25 football fields.

The regional profile also covers extreme weather, institution/complex fires involving less-self-reliant people, dangerous-goods rail/road incidents, tunnel incidents, electricity, drinking-water, telecom/ICT and cyber disruption. These are risk-selection and dependency evidence, not a live incident, municipal probability, dispatch, closure or resource state.

The documents are public policy/governance evidence with explicit adoption/effective dates, regional/municipal narrative coverage and no standard machine-event cadence or reuse licence identified. They cannot generate exact local depth, people, route, service or recovery values.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Samen leven met water 2021–2025 and current climate-adaptation page
evidenceSources.edition: Water policy prepared 31 August 2020 for policy period 2021–2025; current climate page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The expired policy-period document records a mostly combined sewer system routed through principal pumps largely to RWZI Nijverdal, overflows that discharge to the Regge during heavy rain several times per year, separated systems at 't Lochter, a Grotestraat rainwater sewer connected to the city brook and groundwater monitoring/drainage responsibilities.

It distinguishes municipal wastewater, stormwater and groundwater duties; Vechtstromen and Drents Overijsselse Delta surface-water management; water-board wastewater treatment; provincial groundwater permits; and Vitens drinking-water treatment/transport. That establishes multiple owners and dependencies, not current topology or status.

The current page says impermeable urban surfaces prevent infiltration, overburden sewers and retain heat, and names adaptation projects at Kuperserf, central Nijverdal, Noetselerweg, Henri Dunantplein and school grounds. Project naming does not prove completion, performance, connected catchment or availability during an event.

The PDF and pages are documentary evidence with local but non-exhaustive coverage, policy/project dates, no machine event cadence and no standard redistribution licence found. They support mechanism review; live pipes, inlets, overflows, pumps, groundwater, capacity and restoration remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Twents Waternet / Waterschap Vechtstromen / Province of Overijssel and fourteen participating municipalities
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Klimaatatlas Twente public climate-stress catalogue and methodology
evidenceSources.edition: Regional climate stress test assembled in 2019; public catalogue inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The official atlas covers water nuisance, heat, drought and flooding across the fourteen Twente municipalities and is intended for risk dialogue and adaptation planning. Its public catalogue exposes map layers and visualization interfaces, not current conditions.

The methodology states that the upper short-duration extreme-rain maps are joint worst-case products in which sewer drainage is not included; lower maps can be older municipality-supplied stress tests. Different products and assumptions must not be blended or treated as observed water.

Raster download requires data-owner permission and authentication; Nelen & Schuurmans is not the owner. The public atlas does not state one blanket standard reuse licence, native resolution, fixed refresh cadence or uniform NoData contract. Data.overheid exposes some separate 2019 Twents Waternet layers as public-domain, but licence must be resolved per layer.

The atlas is a modeled design-screening evidence class. A causal adapter must retain owner, layer/scenario, edition, rainfall/duration, included drainage, CRS, native resolution, units, coverage, NoData, licence and uncertainty and must never call it a T+0 observation.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Hellendoornse Berg fire-safety project, official combustible-nature polygon and Sallandse Heuvelrug access context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal project intended from autumn 2025; Risicokaart metadata updated 19 February 2026 with polygon validity from 9 March 2005; access page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality planned a 20 m north–south fire-safety strip across Hellendoornse Berg and strips near Avonturenpark Hellendoorn and care location Krönnenzommer, using pruning, removal of conifers/dead wood and planting/retention of deciduous vegetation. Intended start and landowner consent do not prove completed protection.

The public IPO WFS identifies Nationaal Park Sallandse Heuvelrug as a 5,200 ha mixed-forest/heath combustible area supplied by Hellendoorn. A reproducible WFS point query at [6.42, 52.39] intersects this polygon and the generated neighbourhood Hellendoorn.

Data.overheid lists the nature-fire dataset as Public Domain; metadata was updated 19 February 2026, while the Hellendoorn feature's begin-validity is 9 March 2005 and no guaranteed operational feature cadence or current fuel state is stated. It is eligibility/context, not an ignition or perimeter.

Staatsbosbeheer places the approximately 5,200 ha National Park between Hellendoorn and Holten, with public access generally between sunrise and sunset and time-dependent motor-vehicle restrictions on through roads. Visitor/access pages are context, not event-time occupancy, responder access, closure or throughput.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — N35 Salland-Twentetunnel, NWB roads, rail stations, scheduled transit and current road situations
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; current RWS tunnel page; ProRail/GTFS/NDW snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: Rijkswaterstaat identifies the N35 as the Zwolle–Wierden corridor and the Salland-Twentetunnel in Nijverdal as a 493 m combined road/rail tunnel with one two-track rail tube and two one-lane road tubes, monitored and operated 24/7 from Wolfheze. Static design does not prove current opening or capacity.

The generated monthly CC0 NWB graph includes six N347/N750/N751/N835 logical edges to Twenterand, Wierden, Ommen and Raalte but no N35 edge in either direction and no tunnel object. Nominal 150 values are scenario units, and secondary routes cannot silently substitute for the omitted corridor.

ProRail's CC0 register places stations at Nijverdal and Daarlerveen, and GTFS supplies 43 stop areas. Static rail/station geometry and best-effort schedule validity do not establish running trains/buses, passengers, evacuation throughput, accessibility, freight, tunnel availability or recovery.

The CC0 NDW snapshot assigns zero current situations to GM0163. This is no matching covered record at publication time, never proof that N35, the tunnel, regional/local roads, level crossings, rail or transit are open. Registers, schedules and timestamped situations retain distinct evidence classes.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards; Netbeheer Nederland; RDI; DUO; RIVM; Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, electricity planning, antennas, education, air quality, acute care and Waterinfo context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; HWH contributor dates vary; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Full-boundary containment assigns 134 HWH CC BY-SA 4.0 records to GM0163: three sewer pumps, eight surface-water pumps, RWZI Nijverdal and 122 weirs. Eighty-five list Vechtstromen, 45 Drents Overijsselse Delta, one generic Waterschap and three no manager. Contributor completeness varies and a point is not hydraulic topology, live control or capacity proof.

One postcode-level NBNL planning sample identifies Enexis NVD Nijverdal: 87.2 MW existing withdrawal and injection, withdrawal 41.2 MW required/6.6 MW queued/34 requests, injection 38.5 MW required/2.5 MW queued/21 requests, TenneT classes 3/3 and thirteen projects, earliest 2026. Its exact dataset licence is unstated and one sample is not municipal/feeder coverage, outage or reserve.

The context assigns 78 RDI antenna records—40 mobile, fifteen fixed, one other-mobile and 22 amateur—and 25 daily CC-BY DUO education locations. The RDI WFS states no standard reuse licence/cadence. Points do not establish radio coverage/backhaul/power, pupils, shelter role, staffing, stocks or availability.

One indicative RIVM hourly station measured PM2.5 6.45 µg/m³ at Hellendoorn-Luttenbergerweg for 2026-09-02T17:00Z; RIVM states no standard reuse licence for this service. Zero RIVM acute-care, Waterinfo, KNMI station, KNMI seismic-origin and NDW matches mean no record in each scope, not zero care, water, weather, seismic risk or road disruption. All remain affectsSimulation=false.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Adopted Zorgrisicoprofiel Twente 2025 and dated acute-care questionnaire
evidenceSources.edition: Care-risk profile 2025 adopted 23 April 2026; RIVM acute-care version 1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The adopted profile says Twente's acute hospitals are in Enschede, Almelo, Hengelo and Oldenzaal, while much care operates in rural areas; older people, independently living less-self-reliant people and home medical-device users are vulnerable to power, water and internet interruption.

It records the November 2022 Krönnenzommer fire in Hellendoorn: 66 clients were evacuated and one went to hospital. The analysis identifies transport, coordination, patient registration, alternative placement, staffing, smoke evacuation and return-to-care planning as limitations. This is retrospective evidence, not current occupancy or readiness.

The profile prioritizes cybercrime, energy interruption and fire in a facility with less-self-reliant occupants and keeps drink-water contamination relevant. It also notes extreme rain can impede access to care via flooded streets or tunnels. Planning concerns do not generate exact current capacity or routes.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 is a dated national CC0 questionnaire and has zero respondent locations inside GM0163. This means no covered SEH point intersects the boundary, not no local care or demand; live acceptance, beds, staffing, diversion, backup and ambulance travel remain Unknown.

identity.summary: GM0163, Hellendoorn, Overijssel and Veiligheidsregio Twente agree across generated and official 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature id, municipality bundle code/name, province, safety region and 2025 boundary/statistics editions agree.
The generated centre and all five BAG place centres lie inside the generalized municipality boundary.
No identity, regional-membership or headline-population contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is coherent but cannot resolve Regge/sewer flow, Sallandse Heuvelrug fire, tunnel or service footprints.
notes: All 39 neighbourhoods belong to GM0163; five BAG places and 23 BRT settlements cover the urban, village and dispersed-rural pattern.
Regge, city-brook, overflows, groundwater, terrain, mixed forest/heath, N35 tunnel approaches and two water-board territories require full-resolution mechanism-specific geometry.
Municipality/neighbourhood centres and settlement labels cannot select a flood cell, sewer catchment, ignition, visitor location, tunnel state, facility or service area.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals and neighbourhood values reconcile within CBS publication precision.
notes: Official/generated population is 36,213, density 263/km², age 65+ is 24.3% and one-person households number 4,441.
Neighbourhood population sums to 36,190, 23 below the municipality (-0.064%); households sum to 15,040 and age-65-plus rows to 8,790.
Older-person share is planning context, not an individual label. Residents exclude tourists, park visitors, patients, staff, pupils, rail/road users, responders and displaced people.

regionalDetail.summary: All 39 neighbourhoods and 36 statistic fields are retained, but partial values and synthetic priorities limit operational use.
notes: Most demographic fields are complete; several housing/access/benefit fields are missing for one neighbourhood and cars per household for three.
District heating and charging are unavailable in all 39 and correctly remain null rather than zero.
Kruidenwijk Oost, Noetsele I, Groot Lochter, De Blokken and Kruidenwijk Noord are the largest published neighbourhoods, but resident size alone cannot set flood, fire, care or response priority.
Transient tourism, Avonturenpark/National Park visitors, care residents, employees and transport users have no timestamped occupancy input.

settlements.summary: Five BAG places and 23 BRT settlements are represented without treating labels as operational areas.
notes: BAG identifies Daarle, Daarlerveen, Haarle, Hellendoorn and Nijverdal; BRT adds six woonkernen, fifteen buurtschappen and two gehuchten.
No generated BAG place centre is outside the generalized boundary and no foreign/inactive place is present.
Settlement membership does not establish present population, Regge compartment, nature-fire perimeter, tunnel/access zone, care catchment or lifeline topology.

transport.summary: The six-edge graph omits Hellendoorn's defining N35 and combined road/rail tunnel dependency.
notes: Generated edges cover N347/N750/N751/N835 to four neighbours, all at nominal 150 scenario units, but omit N35 west toward Raalte/Zwolle and east toward Wierden/Almelo.

Rijkswaterstaat/VRT identify the 493 m Salland-Twentetunnel in Nijverdal as the only long tunnel in Twente, combining two road tubes and a two-track rail tube under 24/7 remote operation. It has no graph node/state or shared-failure relationship.
Nijverdal and Daarlerveen stations plus 43 GTFS stop areas are static/scheduled context and cannot substitute for incident-time road/rail access, passengers, evacuation or supply throughput.
Zero NDW situations means no matching record at the retrieval time, not that N35, the tunnel, roads, crossings or transit are open.

emergencyContext.summary: Material water, nature-fire, care, tunnel and lifeline evidence remains non-causal, with no governed action state for T+0–72.
notes: Context includes 134 public water assets, 25 education locations, 78 antenna records, one air station, one electricity-planning sample and zero RIVM acute-care locations; every family retains its register/observation/planning role and does not affect simulation.

The municipality documents Regge overflows, multi-owner water duties and proposed/adaptation measures; fire strips were intended near the park and Krönnenzommer. These do not prove completed works, live state or incident capacity.

No reviewed public source supplies live shelters, care occupancy/acceptance, visitors, crews, tunnel/rail operation, water controls, physical utility topology, backup endurance, fuel, stocks, household preparedness or restoration commitments. These remain Unknown or security-sensitive.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services with finite output.
notes: Focused reproduction used MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0163 pnpm audit:model; one file and two tests passed over the complete 10 × 6 × 8 contract.

Peak checkpoint severity / maximum affected / T+72 event-attributable deprived person-hours are: severe storm 0.574728 / 9,637 / 409,211.480; pluvial 0.375932 / 7,096 / 386,804.714; river 0.255632 / 9,751 / 767,510.247; coastal 0.067670 / 0 / 178,253.200; heat 0.458109 / 793 / 169,636.970.

Coastal direct inundation is zero and the preset is an inland wind exercise; canonical wildfire has zero direct flame, and earthquake is a remote-source exercise. Outputs are deterministic indices/people-equivalent, not observations, probabilities, measured depth, casualties or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All service availability remains in [0,1]; hazard dimensions, demand, delivery, affected people-equivalent and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero-intensity scenarios return exact zero severity, affected population and event-attributable burden; repeated runs are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.

Every service allocates all 39 neighbourhoods and reconciles exactly to 36,213 residents; local affected, demand and delivery close to municipality values and selected map layers leave the scenario invariant.
Passing arithmetic validates internal computation only, not local source, spatial allocation, topology or restoration precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A shared seeded rank and failed source containment contradict Hellendoorn's water and nature-fire geography.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire use the exact full order: Zeeheldenwijk, Prinsessenwijk, Nijverdal-Centrum, Gagelman Industrieterrein-Noord and Kruidenwijk West lead; Kruidenwijk Oost is last.

A controlled T+11 source at [6.42, 52.39], reproducibly inside both the official Sallandse Heuvelrug combustible polygon and neighbourhood Hellendoorn, creates direct fire 0.763379, smoke 0.749980, severity 0.773292 and 17,334 affected people-equivalent.

Despite the source, neighbourhood Hellendoorn ranks 14/39 and the unchanged common top five lead. The IPO polygon is old-validity eligibility, so the diagnostic is a synthetic exercise rather than a claimed event.
One municipality-id multiplier cannot encode Regge/urban drainage, wind, heat, snow/ice, cyber boundaries, terrain/fuels/smoke and transient visitors. Hotspot precision is unsupported.

serviceDependencies.summary: Service balances calculate but omit the N35 tunnel, physical water chain, acute-care destinations and operator topology.
notes: At compound T+24 availability is power 0.397761, water 0.361688, drainage 0.287927, gas 0.578187, telecom 0.189669, mobility 0.709527, facilities 0.368710 and supply 0.385876.

NWB edges correctly support logical Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply only; they are not physical power, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom or care topology. The omitted N35/tunnel means even mobility/supply coverage is incomplete.

RWZI Nijverdal, three sewer pumps, eight surface-water pumps, 122 weirs, Enexis planning sample, antennas and schools do not supply compatible connectivity, flow/load, controls, current state, backup or repair evidence.

Zero internal RIVM SEH points plus regional hospitals in Almelo/Hengelo/Enschede/Oldenzaal requires explicit care/ambulance destinations and incident-time acceptance, not an exact generic Facilities value.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers close and official context remains non-causal, while local source relevance and actions remain unsupported.
notes: Hazard contributions close to headline severity, ordered service deltas close to availability and weighted service losses close to system pressure; local and municipal demand/delivery reconcile.
Preparedness/intervention changes consequences rather than hazard fragility, and public registers/observations/plans remain affectsSimulation=false.
The trace selects no Regge/Twents Waternet event, local ignition/perimeter, N35/tunnel state, cyber scope, care acceptance, operator topology or authority action/resource.
Arithmetic closure makes the synthetic calculation inspectable; it does not upgrade its evidence class or support precise local decisions.

recovery72h.summary: Standing-water repair blocking is conservative, but exact T+72 effects lack selected footprints, access, owners and resources.
notes: River holds direct stress 0.821737, 9,751 affected people-equivalent, system pressure 0.331124 and all eight service values unchanged from T+24 to T+72, with every recoveryProgress zero under an unselected major-river footprint.
Compound retains flood stress 0.522225 and grows affected from 23,125 to 23,809 and pressure from 0.593251 to 0.606657 while all eight services worsen and recovery remains zero through T+72.

The standing-water guard appropriately prevents generic repair under persistent modeled water, but no recession/dewatering, exposed asset, N35/tunnel access, pump/crew/material/fuel, switching, patient placement or completion state validates the exact timing.
Every deterioration, plateau and restoration at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 needs a typed driver/action/resource ledger with authority, issue/observation/valid time, state and uncertainty.

findings.summary: Generated identity, regional membership, settlements and 2025 demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0163, Hellendoorn, Overijssel, Veiligheidsregio Twente and editions agree; the centre is contained. CBS reports 36,213 residents; 39 neighbourhoods total 36,190 (-0.064%) and reconcile without rewriting observations. Five BAG places, 23 BRT settlements, two stations and 43 stop areas are present.
findings.action: Retain publisher edition/retrieval time, full-resolution geometry access, null semantics, published-versus-allocated reconciliation and register/schedule evidence classes on every refresh.

findings.summary: Unavailable fields and zero locally matched records remain Unknown rather than false zero or safety claims.
findings.evidence: District heating and charging are null for 39/39 neighbourhoods and several fields are partial. Current context has zero internal RIVM acute-care, Waterinfo, KNMI weather-station, KNMI seismic-origin and NDW-situation records. HWH and RDI have provider/register-dependent coverage. No value is fabricated and context remains non-causal.
findings.action: Preserve source version, time, spatial coverage, licence, NoData mask and reason code through ingestion, aggregation, UI and export; never turn an absent field, station, pixel, facility or situation into zero, open/closed or safe.

findings.summary: A national named-major-river screen creates unsupported persistent direct inundation in Hellendoorn.
findings.evidence: River T+24 through T+72 reports direct inundation stress 0.821737, 9,751 affected people-equivalent and 767,510.247 deprived person-hours. findings.action: Suppress direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel amplitude, local exposure and decision-facing percentages for GM0163. Keep Regge/brooks, pluvial/sewer/groundwater and indirect IJssel-region effects Unknown until Vechtstromen/WDOD/VRT select a versioned scenario with valid-time and spatial support.

findings.summary: Generic pluvial forcing omits local sewer overflow, terrain, brook, groundwater and two-water-board pathways.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports stress 0.506467, 7,096 affected and Drainage 0.475630. The municipal plan documents a mostly combined system, principal pumps to RWZI Nijverdal, heavy-rain overflows to the Regge and city-brook/groundwater systems. Twents Waternet offers scenario layers but warns the joint worst-case short-rain maps omit sewer drainage. None supplies this exact footprint or service state.
findings.action: Select and ingest compatible Twents Waternet/authority scenarios with KNMI rainfall, AHN terrain and governed municipal GWSW/overflow/pump/groundwater plus Vechtstromen/WDOD water topology. Retain scenario, rainfall/duration, included drainage, units, CRS, resolution, NoData, licence, coverage, issue/valid time and uncertainty.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated individual hazards reuse one exact 39-neighbourhood rank.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire rank Zeeheldenwijk, Prinsessenwijk, Nijverdal-Centrum, Gagelman Industrieterrein-Noord and Kruidenwijk West first through fifth and Kruidenwijk Oost last. The order is invariant despite incompatible physical sources and despite official water/nature geography.
findings.action: Replace the shared region-id multiplier with hazard-specific versioned surfaces and uncertainty. Suppress hotspot/rank language and mark local values unsupported until each municipality-hazard pair has selected event/source/time/geometry evidence.

findings.summary: A source inside the official Sallandse Heuvelrug polygon fails to prioritize its containing neighbourhood.
findings.evidence: A controlled T+11 ignition at [6.42, 52.39] lies inside the official 5,200 ha mixed-forest/heath polygon and generated neighbourhood Hellendoorn. It produces direct fire 0.763379, smoke 0.749980, severity 0.773292 and 17,334 affected people-equivalent, but Hellendoorn ranks 14/39 while the common urban top five lead. Canonical wildfire itself has zero direct flame at T+24.
findings.action: Keep the canonical preset labelled remote smoke/drought and add a named local nature-fire exercise using IPO eligibility, event-valid KNMI weather, current fuel/moisture, visitor/care exposure, access, response water and authority ignition/perimeter/suppression. If live inputs are unavailable, use the smallest explicit synthetic perimeter and require source containment.

findings.summary: The graph omits N35 in both directions and the Salland-Twentetunnel's coupled road/rail failure mode.
findings.evidence: The generated network has six N347/N750/N751/N835 border links but no N35 west to Raalte/Zwolle or east to Wierden/Almelo. RWS and VRT identify the 493 m Nijverdal tunnel as a combined two-track rail/dual road-tube structure and Twente's only long tunnel, under 24/7 control. Two station points, schedules and secondary roads cannot represent its availability, detours or shared incident.
findings.action: Add audited N35 west/east edges and a typed tunnel asset linking road and rail with direction/mode, physical capacity ceiling, portal/access, monitoring owner, incident/closure state, emergency priority, detours and valid time. Never infer opening from zero NDW matches or automatically transfer a road restriction to rail without mode-specific evidence.

findings.summary: Partial water points and an expired policy document cannot support exact Water/Drainage topology or restoration.
findings.evidence: Public HWH containment returns three sewer pumps, eight surface-water pumps, RWZI Nijverdal and 122 weirs across Vechtstromen, WDOD and incomplete manager fields. The 2021–2025 municipal plan documents many additional network classes and connected Regge overflows but is not a current complete asset export. Exact Water/Drainage values consume no compatible pipe/catchment/control/backup state.
findings.action: Request governed current municipal GWSW and Vechtstromen/WDOD/WBL-style wastewater and regional-water topology with asset identity, direction, catchment, compatible capacity units, telemetry/control time, power/backup, condition and restoration. Reconcile public HWH coverage explicitly and leave absent components Unknown.

findings.summary: Care evacuation, external acute care and National Park/Avonturenpark visitors lack live exposure, capacity and routes.
findings.evidence: The care profile records 66 Krönnenzommer clients evacuated in 2022 and identifies transport, staffing, placement, registration and return planning limitations. The municipal fire project names Krönnenzommer and Avonturenpark as vulnerable locations. RIVM returns no internal acute hospital and VRT places acute hospitals elsewhere in Twente. Static residents, 25 schools and visitor pages do not capture current people, destinations or acceptance.
findings.action: Add authority-reviewed aggregate care, recreation and tourist exposure with observation/valid time plus facilities/destinations, role, activation, staffing/capacity range, patient/client needs, transport, acceptance/diversion, shelter, backup and accessible alternatives. Never convert historical evacuation or zero SEH records into current readiness or zero demand.

findings.summary: Exact weather, cyber, seismic and lifeline consequences lack local event fields and physical system boundaries.
findings.evidence: At T+24 affected people-equivalent are 9,637 storm, zero coastal, 793 heat, 14,949 winter, 10,913 cyber and zero earthquake. No issue/valid-time KNMI field, heat/exposure surface, winter route/gritting state, authorised cyber boundary or local earthquake source is selected. One RIVM air observation, one NBNL planning sample and 78 antenna points cannot validate exact power/water/gas/telecom/facility consequences.
findings.action: Require a municipality-hazard-service support matrix with event/source, issue/valid time, spatial/system boundary, exposed objects, uncertainty and licence. Use authorised privacy/security-safe operator zones/outage/restoration ranges where possible; otherwise retain versioned synthetic ranges. Coastal zero remains only a narrow direct North-Sea result, not an all-flood all-clear.

findings.summary: First-72-hour service plateaus and recovery are not tied to named actions, resources, tunnel access or operators.
findings.evidence: River freezes all eight services from T+24 to T+72 with recoveryProgress zero under unsupported water. Compound retains water, grows affected from 23,125 to 23,809 and pressure from 0.593251 to 0.606657 while every service worsens and recovery remains zero. residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, fire forecast, tunnel operating decision, hospital status or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and residents exclude tourists, Avonturenpark/National Park visitors, commuters, pupils, patients, staff, road/rail users, responders and displaced people; no timestamped occupancy is consumed.

Generalized polygons and centroids cannot resolve Regge/brook flow, terrain, sewer/groundwater catchments, combustible vegetation, visitor/care exposure, N35/tunnel approaches or utility/service zones.

The Twente profile supports suppressing generic named-major-river direct precision, not declaring Hellendoorn flood-safe. Local Regge, brook, heavy-rain, groundwater, sewer/overflow and indirect IJssel-region effects remain unresolved.

The Twents Waternet atlas is modeled design-screening with product-specific assumptions; the joint worst-case short-rain map omits sewer drainage. Raster download needs owner permission and no blanket licence, resolution, cadence or NoData contract applies across layers.

Hellendoorn's 2021–2025 water plan is expired policy-period evidence. It documents system classes and historic operating behavior but not a complete 2026 topology, asset state, capacity, telemetry, backup or restoration.

HWH point coverage is partial/provider-dependent across two water boards and unknown manager fields. Registered or realised does not establish connectivity, current operation, compatible capacity, power, controls or recovery.

IPO nature polygons use old feature-validity and identify eligibility, not current fuel/moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke, visitors, access, water supply, crews or suppression. The controlled source is synthetic.
The planned fire-safety strip and measures near Avonturenpark/Krönnenzommer do not prove landowner approval, completion, condition or incident performance at the simulation time.

NWB, ProRail, GTFS, RWS pages and NDW do not establish scenario-time N35/tunnel/rail/bus state, capacity, passengers, emergency priority, detour throughput or restoration. Zero current situations is no record, not open infrastructure.

The Krönnenzommer 2022 evacuation is retrospective. RIVM's zero internal acute-care respondent locations does not erase local care or demand, and regional hospital registers do not establish live acceptance, beds, staffing, ambulance routes or backup.

One NBNL postcode sample, RDI antennas, DUO schools and RIVM air station are planning/register/observation context. They do not establish customer connectivity, network coverage, occupancy, shelter role, load, outage, reserve or repair.

Complete physical power, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply and emergency-resource topology, live state, backup, stock, crew and restoration data may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remain Unknown or explicitly synthetic.
Zero local KNMI station/seismic, Waterinfo, acute-care or NDW matches reflect bounded dataset coverage/time only and never mean zero weather, seismic hazard, water, care need or road disruption.

Exact hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service-availability, recovery and deprived-person-hour values remain synthetic/derived exercise outputs until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the selected event; impacts beyond T+72 are outside scope.
